detail.description: Agency: Department of the Army Office: Army Contracting Command, Edgewood Contracting Division Location: Fort Detrick, MD, USA Program Office: Capability Program Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (CPE CBRN Defense), Joint Project Lead Enabling Technologies (JPL ET) RPP Number: W911SR-26-R-CADENCC Date Issued: 03 September 2026 Proposals Due: 1500 hours, 17 September 2026 1. Through this Request for Project Proposal (RPP), the Capability Program Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense’s (CPE CBRN Defense) Joint Project Lead Enabling Technologies (JPL ET) seeks to develop Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Advance Defense Enabling Network and Clinical Capability (CADENCC), an enabling capability that will accelerate clinical trial startup through implementation of Master Protocols, innovative technologies that support decentralized trial operations and augment data collection and analysis, and establishment of a pre-positioned clinical trial site network enabling CBRN defense readiness as described in the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). The Government is hereby requesting formal submission of preproposals to execute a formal agreement under 10 USC 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for the prototype project described below. Upon receipt of a preproposal submitted in response to this RPP, the next steps are as follows: The Government will evaluate the preproposal. Discussions among the parties, whether verbally or in writing, will occur as appropriate. The Government may request a full proposal from the offeror. Additional discussions will occur as necessary. Award may be made after evaluation and selection of a successful submission. (Note: Awards are dependent upon the availability of funds.) 2. This RPP is issued to request project proposals in compliance with USC 4022 and is being issued for planning purposes only. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to award an agreement, nor will the Government pay for the information solicited. 3. The JPL ET enables the rapid development, manufacture, and fielding of safe and effective medical solutions across the full product spectrum, including development, clinical trials, manufacturing, and validated biological threat detection materials. The objective of Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Advance Defense Enabling Network and Clinical Capability (CADENCC) is to develop an enabling capability that will accelerate clinical trial startup through implementation of Master Protocols, innovative technologies that support decentralized trial operations and augment data collection and analysis, and establishment of a pre-positioned clinical trial site network enabling CBRN defense readiness. CADENCC will primarily conduct Phase I/Phase II clinical trials for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and early treatment products which may be under Animal Rule. Any resultant award may be issued as a prototype Agreement under the authority of 10 USC 4022, with the expectation that quantities necessary for production, including fielding and testing new capabilities, may be non-competitively procured from awarded to the successful performer(s) of a prototype project in a follow-on production contract or other transaction agreement. 4. detail.title: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE: DESIGN-BUILD TO BUDGET (DB2B) Airborne Equipment Parachute Repair Shop, Yuma Proving Ground, Yuma, Arizona
detail.description: Pre-Solication notice change 0001: The purpose of this change is to notify prospective offerors of a revision to the anticipated project scope of work: The anticipated facility size is revised from approximately 13,000SF down to approximately 10,315 SF. PRESOLICITATION NOTICE (SYNOPSIS): DESIGN-BUILD TO BUDGET (DB2B) Airborne Equipment Parachute Repair Shop, Yuma Proving Ground, Yuma, Arizona The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Los Angeles District, intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the design and construction of the Airborne Equipment Parachute Repair Shop (Airdrop Rigging Facility) located at Yuma Proving Ground (YPG) in Yuma, Arizona. This procurement is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. Proposed Solicitation Number : W912PL26RA046 Product Service Code (PSC): Y1EZ – Construction of Other Industrial Buildings NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Small Business Size Standard: $45.0 Million Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type : Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Procurement Method : Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures (in accordance with RFO FAR Subpart 36) Acquisition Strategy : Design-Build to Budget (DB2B) Best Value Tradeoff Process SCOPE OF WORK: The anticipated scope of work is for a complete design-build solution for a new, approximately 10,315 square foot climate-controlled Airdrop Rigging Facility. The facility must constructed in close proximity to the existing airdrop rigging, parachute repair facilities and aircraft loading site, to allow for environmentally controlled storage and inspection of rigged materials prior to airdrop. The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: Complete Design & Compliance: Develop a complete design that complies with DoD antiterrorism/force protection requirements (UFC 4-010-01) and ensures a minimum facility life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated building systems performance). Site Work & Utilities: Perform all site work to prepare the building site and account for storm drainage, including moderate site grading, demolition and relocation of an existing fire access lane, connection to nearby utilities, and the construction of a new septic system for sanitary sewer. This section also incorporates the full design, procurement, structural/electrical provisions, and installation of a overhead 50-ton crane. Facility Features: Construct the facility to include a partially raised loading dock, motorized roll-up doors, and specialized storage rooms with adequate spacing for tools, materials, and the joint inspection of materials within the building envelope. Aircraft Cargo Conveyance: Integrate a military aircraft cargo conveyance roller system (compatible with C-130 and C-17 cargo configurations) installed inside multiple high-bay rigging lanes, with the final quantity, layout, and configuration of lanes optimized by the Contractor to maximize throughput and rigging capacity within the fixed budget ceiling. Climate Control HVAC: Install all necessary facility climate-control systems, including self-contained cooling and heating HVAC systems (estimated at 170 tons of capacity) to maintain strict temperature and humidity parameters. Communications & Security: Provide complete communications infrastructure, conduits with pull strings placed under new roadways for future communication installations, and a closed-circuit television (CCTV) system. detail.description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). detail.title: HMEE IV FOLLOW-ON EFFORT
detail.description: The U.S. Army is seeking information to assess the availability of sources to meet the Government’s requirement for the High Mobility Engineer Excavator (HMEE). The HMEE Type IV capability, outlined within AUTOMOTIVE TANK PURCHASE DESCRIPTION-2301A, is a pneumatic tired, diesel-engine driven, all-wheel drive tractor with attachments, for excavation of small emplacements, material handling, and general construction tasks; with tactical mobility over rough terrain and high mobility on roadways. The basic tractor, is classified as a self-propelled construction vehicle, meeting federal highway safety standards as well as emission standards for Non-Road Engines. Emissions standards follow exemption Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Section 89.908(a)1. The Type I tractor is equipped with a front loader attachment; a rear mounted backhoe; portable tools; and when specified, provisions for an Army radio set. The HMEE Type IV is conveyable by rail, marine, highway and air modes of transportation. The objective of this Sources Sought Questionnaire is to better understand the availability and capabilities of Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) or other sources for vehicle systems meeting the HMEE requirements, ancillary equipment, and system services. The Army plans on procuring an estimated 360 HMEEs over a minimum of five, and a maximum of 10, one-year periods and plans to establish Firm Fixed Price (FFP) pricing for each period. The quantities identified and length of contract are not binding and are subject to change. The information gathered by the Army through this questionnaire, along with other market investigation data, is solely intended for use by the U.S. Army and will not be shared amongst competing companies. For instructions and more information regarding proprietary information, please refer to Section IV of this document. Participation in this Sources Sought Questionnaire by the various contractors is considered low risk to the commercial companies, as responses will be treated per Section IV as proprietary.

detail.title: Sand Trail Phase II
detail.description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1240BJ26Q0021 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This project is located on the Cordova Ranger District. This contract aims to repair and mitigate future failures of the USFS Sand Trail infrastructure, trail number 229. The total trail length is 12.20 miles long; this contract will only address the first 1.70 miles of failing trail. The mitigation consists of installing bank armoring with rip rap, and placing sub grade aggregate along the trail. The sub grade aggregate (3” minus) is to be placed as backfill behind the riprap and is incidental to item 201501A. Backfill quantities will vary but the end product is to have ~2-4 ft of 3” minus behind the placed riprap. The D-1 aggregate is to be placed on the trail running surface to harden the trail for ATV use. The majority of trail 229 is 6 to 8 feet in width and will require additional clearing and minor excavation depending on type of equipment used. Construction must occur during low water times of year, diversion of smaller channels within the project location will be needed to dewater bank locations. Small diversion for bank armoring is assumed to be conducted with either a dozer or excavator that may operate in the stream channel or along the stream bank. Work must be performed when there is 5 consecutive days below 30F degrees are reached This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard is $45,000,000.00 This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

detail.title: FY28 Frequency Converter Plant, Yokohama North Dock
detail.description: See attachment for full Market Questionnaire. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is exploring the use of alternative acquisition strategies like Progressive Design Build and Integrated Design and Construction for the upcoming electrical substation project at Yokohama North Dock. Because these contracting method differ from traditional U.S. Government Fixed-Price Design-Build contracts, this summary is provided to explain the different framework, how risks are shared, and how the contractor and Government will collaborate as well as to determine local industry interest in these new methods. What is Progressive Design-Build (PDB)? PDB is a highly collaborative project delivery method. Unlike traditional Design-Build where contractors must submit a final construction proposal based on an incomplete preliminary design, PDB selects a contractor based primarily on their qualifications, past performance, and expertise, rather than a final price. What is Integrated Design & Construction (IDAC)? The Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC) acquisition strategy represents a highly collaborative, two-phase procurement method designed to mitigate risks, compress timelines, and control costs on complex military and civil works construction projects. The intent is to competitively select the construction contractor early in the design cycle. This allows the construction contractor to provide real-time constructability reviews, cost estimations, and market supply-chain analysis while the Designer of Record (DOR) finalizes the design. For both methods, once the contractor is selected, the U.S. Government and the Contractor work together as a team to collaboratively/progressively develop the design, schedule, and cost. detail.title: M456 AND M458 DETONATING CORDS
detail.description: SOURCES SOUGHT FOR M456 AND M458 DETONATING CORDS INTRODUCTION The U.S. Army Contracting Command – Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of the Office of the Project Manager for Close Combat Systems (OPM-CCS) is conducting a Market Survey to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing and delivering 3000 FT – CORD, DETONATING: TYPE I, CLASS E, M456 (Department of Defense Identification Code M456, NSN 1375-00-180-9356), the CORD, DETONATING, REINFORCED, M456 (Department of Defense Identification Code M456, NSN 1375-00-028-5168), and 3000 FT – DUMMY CORD, DETONATING: INERT, M458 (Department of Defense Identification Code M458, NSN 1375-00-621-8373). Based on the responses to this Sources Sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. Multiple awards may be made. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding submissions. DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. PROGRAM/SYSTEM DESCRIPTION DODIC: M456 3000 FT – CORD, DETONATING: TYPE I, CLASS E P/N 13042069 / NSN: 1375-00-180-9356 Type I Class E Detonating Cord consists of a minimum core of 50 grains per foot of PETN per MIL-DTL-387 with an optional center string, protected by layers of material: an optional paper liner, braided or counter wrapped textile, and an olive drab plastic sheath. The cord has a maximum diameter of 0.235 inches. The cord has a detonating velocity of not less than 5,900 meters per second and is waterproof. DODIC: M456 CORD, DETONATING, REINFORCED P/N 2114302 / NSN: 1375-00-028-5168 Type I Class M Detonating Cord (Reinforced) consists of the same construction as Type I Class E with an additional, outer layer of wax coated textile, while having a maximum diameter of 0.225 inches.[MB1] DODIC: M458 DUMMY CORD, DETONATING: INERT P/N 13042070 / NSN: 1375-00-621-8373 Type III Inert Detonating Cord is similar to Type 1, Class E in construction and external appearance and consists of an asphalt coated cotton tube sheathed in an outer cover of smooth plastic-coated rayon. However, it is inert loaded with polyvinyl chloride (PVC) filler and the plastic outer coat is either blue or bronze. The primary use of Detonating Cord is to prime and detonate other explosive charges, although it is also used in urban breaching operations. The M458 Inert Detonating Cord is used in demonstration and training for demolitions and does not perform any ballistic function. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The Government requires the manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of the three types of Detonating Cord in accordance with the Government owned Technical Data Packages (TDPs). The respondent must have available most of the skills, facilities, and equipment to manufacture, test/inspect, and deliver the Detonating Cord. Specific manufacturing capabilities include but are not limited to explosive and pyrotechnic processing, loading and Load Assemble Pack (LAP) of the final products. First Article Testing (FAT) as well as Conformance/Lot Acceptance Testing (LAT) at the component and end-item level to include physical measurements and functional testing will be required. detail.title: GAOA LDV Crystal Lakes Water & Septic Resuscitation, PSICC, Colorado

This SF30 must be acknowledged and submitted with your proposal. ****************************************************************************************************************************************************** This project involves installing a new 2-inch HDPE waterline beneath Colorado Highway 24, including completing all Subsurface Utility Engineering required for CDOT permitting. Work includes connecting the new waterline from Dwelling 1 to the existing distribution system, replacing the well pump to provide a 15 GPM supply, installing a dual‑stage booster pump and basement water storage, and performing associated electrical upgrades such as relocating meters, burying service lines, upgrading panels, and supporting septic and booster pump systems. The NAICS code for this procurement is 532412. *NOTE: If interested firms find a different NAICS code is more suitable for the type of work mentioned, they are urged to include suggested NAICS in the capabilities package. * The project is planned to be issued in the FALL of 2026 with work to take place in the WINTER/SPRING of 2027. Key work components of the Performance Work Statement may include: Furnishing and operating critical maritime and heavy equipment assets. detail.description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) - B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement or contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) or Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Procurement Process: Early involvement, separate contracts, guaranteed maximum price and collaborative delivery. PROJECT OVERVIEW & SCOPE. Title: B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar Location: Dyess Air Force Base, Texas Scope: Construct a new 95,529 sq. ft. Low Observable Corrosion Control Hangar (LO) and a Radio Frequency Facility (RF) for the new B-21 weapons system. The project demands a highly collaborative and iterative design process to manage complexity and a critical schedule. detail.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION - Exploring Innovative Design and Construction Methodologies with Korean Industry
detail.description: SPECIAL NOTICE – REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AMENDMENT 01 USACE FED plans to hold a Reverse Industry Day on 6 October 2026. The exact time and location will be announced separately to interested companies. Information received in response to this RFI will help USACE FED prepare for the event and identify topics that will support meaningful discussions with industry in Korea. The Reverse Industry Day will provide an opportunity for USACE FED and Industry to openly exchange information and learn from each other regarding innovative or non-traditional acquisition and project delivery methods, as well as real-world experiences and lessons learned in improving project delivery timelines and controlling costs. 1. Purpose Currently, USACE FED is looking for better ways to manage projects, improve project timelines, and control costs. To do this, we are exploring innovative and non-traditional methods such as: Progressive Design-Build (PDB): The project scope and price are developed in stages collaboratively between the Government and the Design-Build firm as a team. The team work closely together to define the project before setting a final price, and allows for the Design-Build firm to progress to construction, non-competitively. Other Transaction Authority (OTA) as a procurement method for the Government: A flexible U.S. Government contracting method that allows for faster and more innovative solutions, by reducing some standard contracting rules. Agreements resulting from OTA is legally binding instrument, other than a procurement contract, that is not subject to FAR and supplements. It enables commercial style business arrangements. Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR): A delivery method in which the constructor joins the design process early, collaborating with the designer to establish a guaranteed maximum price (GMP) and completes construction. *See supplemental information attached to this notice. We invite all interested companies in design, engineering, construction, architecture-engineering, and project management with relevant experience and expertise in Korea. This includes companies with strong experience in private sector or Korean Government projects. You do not need prior experience with the U.S. Government or with our acquisition procedures. We want to learn about your successful methods and how they work. 2. Information Requested To help USACE FED better understand Korean industry capabilities and prepare for a meaningful and productive Reverse Industry Day on 6 October 2026, the Government has identified the questions and discussion topics below for consideration by industry. These questions represent areas that USACE FED may discuss with industry during the Reverse Industry Day. Interested companies are encouraged to review the questions in advance, consider how their experience and capabilities relate to these topics, and come prepared to share their perspectives, experiences, lessons learned, and recommendations during the event. Companies are not required to provide written responses to every question. The intent is to provide industry with advance visibility into the Government's areas of interest and allow participants sufficient time to prepare for a meaningful Government-industry exchange. Describe your company's capability and experience in delivering large or complex design and construction projects in Korea. detail.title: The Data COUNTS™ (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times)
detail.description: Description This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or questions. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain knowledge and information for project planning purposes. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The NIH seeks information on technologies and capabilities to further the objectives of the Data COUNTS program. The Data COUNTS™ (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times) effort is built on collaboration between patients and advocates, government, health systems, technology companies, and the private sector. The Data COUNTS program enables the NIH’s Real-World Data initiative and will provide high quality, standardized data that is provenanced and available through approved access to the research community. The contemplated capability will initially perform requested and approved extraction from Healthcare Partner EMR systems and should be modular and extensible to other authorized source systems such as laboratory information systems, pharmacy information systems, picture archiving and communication systems, vendor-neutral archives, and specialty systems. The Data COUNTS program requires that source data, and source provenance metadata, permissions, and source ontology fields will be preserved without modification or loss. This program will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Technical Requirements of Interest: Address availability and technologies that enable the following features: A durable, Healthcare Partner Leave Behind Technology capability that remains at the Healthcare Partner site after contract completion and can be operated by trained staff without ongoing involvement. The technology should be available and free for use by Healthcare Partners while in the Data COUNTS program. Describe any installation and configuration documentation, operational runbooks, site-controlled credential-transfer procedures, documented dependencies, major-release update procedures, and training that enable independent site operations. Deep query for approved extraction from Healthcare Partner electronic medical records (EMR) systems and other authorized source systems. Capture timestamps and provenance for all data at extraction and maintain an immutable provenance chain. The architecture consumes a machine-readable, version-controlled, authorized, and approved Data Request Specification defining cohort logic, requested source systems, data domains and fields, date range, full or incremental extraction mode, refresh cadence, and applicable authorization and permission rules. Describe how the solution validates data availability against the specification, identifies unavailable or ambiguous fields, avoids silent substitutions, associates the request identifier with each batch and output, and supports reproducible reruns when source data have not changed. An initial automated data quality check validating completeness, uniqueness, data types, date sequencing, and records-per-patient. detail.title: Progressive Design Build (PDB) - Cyber Maintenance Hangar Modernization
detail.description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE Cyber Maintenance Hangar Modernization – Mansfield, OH Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm’s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District plans to issue a solicitation for either the new construction of an ICD-705 compliant endo-skeleton structure within an existing hangar OR new ICD-705 compliant prefabricated panelized facility to house Cyber Warfare Operations within an existing hangar. The project will provide cyber operations space within the existing bay. The awardee will construct all spaces to the appropriate security levels, install communications room to accommodate servers and equipment, provide all supporting electrical, mechanical, security, life safety, fire alarm and sprinkler systems, and communications supporting infrastructure, and provide emergency power systems and standby generator connection. High-Security Spaces (ICD 705): Renovation and construction of Special Access Program (SAP) spaces and Secure Compartmentalized Information Facilities (SCIFs) built to stringent ICD 705 standards along with potential deconstruction of existing Hangar Door to achieve and maintain ICD-705 compliant perimeter. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $50,000,000 (Phase 2) Funding Source: Operations & Maintenance (O&M) 2. PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGY The Government is considering utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement for a prototype project under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies or delivery methodologies to achieve benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The baseline delivery method under consideration is Progressive Design-Build (PDB) . Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government and the OT Awardee will work collaboratively to advance the design, perform constructability reviews, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an "off-ramp" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods. Alternative Under Consideration: The Government is also evaluating a Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) delivery method under the OTA framework, particularly in scenarios where the Government-appointed Architect-Engineer (A-E) / Designer of Record (DOR) is pre-selected and dictated to the constructor. 3. INFORMATION REQUESTED Section 1: Company Profile Firm Name, Address, and Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email). Unique Entity ID (UEI). detail.title: NCI Oncology Clinical Trial System, Management and Support
detail.description: Type of Notice: This is a Small Businesses Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to determine (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service disabled veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; women-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The NAICS code for this acquisition is 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services . The small business size standard is $34M. Background: The Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP), National Cancer Institute (NCI), sponsors and coordinates a broad portfolio of clinical trials evaluating cancer treatments, ranging from early-phase studies to large-scale multi-site trials conducted through national research networks. CTEP relies on a suite of integrated enterprise applications to support protocol and study management, study activation, investigational agent/drug management, safety reporting, regulatory workflows, and data sharing and reporting across a large and diverse community of investigators, sites, and research networks. CTEP’s Enterprise System (CTEP-ESYS) is NCI’s enterprise system environment for supporting the conduct, oversight, and evaluation of NCI-sponsored oncology clinical trials. It provides integrated applications, data repositories, interfaces, and services that support protocol development, study administration, regulatory oversight, user and site credentialing, investigational agent management, safety reporting, data exchange, and operational decision-making across the clinical trials enterprise. Purpose and Objectives: The goal of this acquisition is to identify qualified small business sources capable of providing enterprise-level informatics, application development, modernization, and operational support for CTEP-ESYS environment. The requirement supports complex biomedical, clinical research, healthcare, regulatory, and clinical trial operations, and may include, but is not limited to: Enterprise application operations, maintenance, and enhancement for large-scale, mission-critical enterprise applications and integrated application suites; Custom application development, re-engineering, modernization, and migration, including cloud-based or cloud-first modernization, while maintaining continuity of operations; Clinical trial and biomedical informatics support, including systems for protocol/study management, study activation, trial oversight, investigational agent/drug management, safety reporting, regulatory workflows, and clinical research data management; System integration, interoperability, and data exchange across Government and partner environments, including APIs, interfaces, data pipelines, reporting workflows, and data quality controls; Data management, reporting, analytics, automation, and AI/ML capabilities, including AI-assisted data extraction, classification, summarization, workflow automation, and decision-support tools where outputs support human review rather than replace Government or clinical decision-making; AI-assisted workflow support and governance, including data readiness assessment, model/tool evaluation, validation, monitoring, documentation, and governance of AI/ML-related activities Security, privacy, and compliance support for Federal information systems, including FISMA/NIST-based controls, identity and access management, vulnerability management, ATO support, audit logging, cloud security, backup/disaster recovery, and continuous monitoring; and User support, stakeholder coordination, and program manage

detail.title: Request for Information (RFI) for Navy Collaborative Combat Aircraft Increment 1 Prototype Project
detail.description: 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION & DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION RECEIVED TO INFORM A POTENTIAL PROTOTYPE PROJECT UNDER OTHER TRANSACTION AUTHORITY (OTA), PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C. § 4022. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. ALL INFORMATION SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS RFI IS VOLUNTARY AND THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT COMPENSATE ANY RESPONDENT FOR ANY COST INCURRED IN DEVELOPMENT OF INFORMATION PROVIDED TO THE GOVERNMENT. THIS RFI IS BEING USED AS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL FIRMS CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SUPPLIES DESCRIBED HEREIN PRIOR TO AN ISSUANCE OF A REQUEST FOR WHITE PAPERS (RWP) AND SUBSEQUENT REQUEST FOR PROJECT PROPOSAL (RPP). THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT OBLIGATED TO PAY FOR ANY INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM POTENTIAL SOURCES AS A RESULT OF THIS RFI. THIS DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT OF ANY KIND. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR NON-FAR BASED AGREEMENT (E.G. OTHER TRANSACTION) AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IN RESPONSE TO THIS RFI IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. FAILURE TO SUBMIT A RESPONSE WILL NOT PREVENT A COMPANY FROM PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE COMPETITION RELATED TO THIS REQUIREMENT. CLASSIFICATION OF RESPONSES: ALL SUBMITTED INFORMATION PROVIDED MUST BE UNCLASSIFIED. ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION SUBMITTED MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED AS SUCH AND WILL BE SAFEGUARDED IN ACCORDANCE WITH APPLICABLE GOVERNMENT REGULATIONS. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED MAY BE REVIEWED AND USED ACROSS THE GOVERNMENT. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the Future Advanced Capability Program Office (PMA-228), is seeking industry feedback and capability statements for the Increment 1 (Inc 1) Prototype Development and Demonstration of an affordable, highly capable, risk tolerant, carrier-capable, weaponized, extended range, autonomous unmanned air vehicle that can seamlessly deploy from and recover to Gerald R. Ford-class and Nimitz-class Nuclear Aircraft Carriers (CVN). The Navy Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program was established to provide the Carrier Air Wing (CVW) with lethal, survivable and persistent, versatile platforms capable of operating directly from the sea. As threat networks grow increasingly complex, the Navy must adapt combat strategies by focusing on collaborative manned-unmanned operations, modular open standards, and rapid, cost-effective prototyping. PMA-228, operating under Deputy Portfolio Acquisition Executive (Aviation) Carrier Strike, seeks to execute this carrier-compliant autonomous unmanned air vehicle Inc 1 prototype development and demonstration to significantly reduce technical risk and accelerate capability delivery to the fleet. This prototyping effort addresses key risk reduction activities to evaluate platforms with extended range and payload capacity, while minimizing deck footprint and integrating with established CVN infrastructure. Additionally, it paves the way to provide a future capability to augment 4th and 5th generation aircraft survivability, lethality, and capacity and developing future warfighting capabilities through collaborative Manned-Unmanned Teaming (MUM-T) to ensure the Navy maintains a decisive edge against adversaries. The Government is considering utilizing the Naval Air Systems Consortium (NASC) to potentially award one or more OTAs pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 4022 “Authority of the Department of Defense to carry out certain prototype projects”.

Once cleared, the contractor will remove the old carpet and rubber cove base, managing daily site clean-up and off-base debris disposal, as on-site equipment storage is strictly prohibited. To prepare the space, the contractor will relocate standard furniture --coordinating with the Government to ensure all IT cables, power cords, and personal items are removed beforehand. The installation phase requires laying new, commercial-grade modular carpet tiles or planks directly over the existing vinyl flooring using low-VOC adhesives. The contractor will also install a new vinyl cove base, trim door bottoms for proper clearance, and perform any necessary wall spackling and painting to repair damage caused during the removal of the old baseboards. The project will conclude with the repositioning of all furniture and a final Quality Assurance acceptance inspection conducted by 21 CES Operations Flight personnel. detail.title: Request for Information - Wide-Area IR Persistent Surveillance System
detail.description: This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing Wide Area Infrared Surveillance (WAIS) System. REQUIREMENT Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) 1. Performance & Detection Capabilities • Passive Operation: Provide self-protection and situational awareness without emitting detectable signals. • Detection & Tracking Capacity: Automatically detect and classify up to 100 simultaneous thermal signatures within 1 second. • Detection Ranges: Capable of long-range acquisition across multiple target profiles: • Commercial aircraft up to 93 miles (at 12,000 ft altitude). • Group 2 Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) up to 10 miles. • Personnel and ground vehicles up to 5 miles. • Personnel detection minimum range is 500 meters. • Tracking Accuracy & Reliability: Achieve a 90% overall detection probability. Target tracking accuracy must maintain ±3 degrees at 10 miles and ±5 degrees at 93 miles (evaluated at a 95% confidence level). • Field of View (FOV): The entire system, comprised of multiple sensors, shall provide a minimum of 360° horizontal and 125° vertical hemispherical coverage. • Individual sensors shall have a minimum FOV of 90 degrees. • AI & Automation: Utilize advanced AI/ML-driven algorithms for automated target detection, classification (e.g., distinguishing small drones from commercial airliners), predictive analysis, and pattern recognition. 2. Integration & Interoperability • C2 Integration: Incorporate an open-architecture design to integrate seamlessly with Command and Control (C2) systems, existing Tactical Grid infrastructure, and TACP mission software/hardware. • Sensor Fusion: Capable of fusing multiple passive IR data streams (from within the IRIS-P system), and fusing with active radar and other external EO/IR sensors to deliver comprehensive, multi-domain situational awareness. • Communication Standards: Utilize common tactical interface standards (e.g., MIL-STD-6016) to interface natively with broader electromagnetic spectrum awareness systems. 3. System Operations & Data Management • Usability: Operable by a single user with minimal training. Features a user-friendly laptop workstation interface providing real-time data, tracking options, and automated alerts accessible within 3 seconds of a request. • Operator Verification: Support robust "operator-in-the-loop" workflows to verify, refine, and override automated threat detections. • Networking & Throughput: Process high-fidelity thermal imaging data at a minimum of 1 Gbps throughput on a hard-wired, closed network. Supports real-time data streaming, efficient data compression, and on-demand retrieval. • Security & Storage: Implement role-based and security-clearance-based access control for stored data. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor is it to be construed as a commitment by the U. S. Government to form a binding contract. Parties that respond will not be paid for the information submitted. The Air Force is hereby requesting capability statements and other information from interested sources. General Information: The 412 CS at the Air Force Test Center at Edwards AFB, CA is in the process of determining the acquisition strategy to obtain information from potential eligible and interested contractors for the purchase of FES Hovercraft. The AFTC anticipates awarding a contract under the associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) is 336612 with a standard employee size of 1000 and a Product Service Code (PSC) of 1940. A firm-fixed price contract will be contemplated. Salient Characteristics (Minimum Government Technical Requirements) Requirement Category -Minimum Acceptable Threshold (Government Minimum Need) Braking & Maneuverability -Must feature an active reverse-thrust braking system capable of redirecting at least 50–60% of engine thrust forward via fly-by-wire/cockpit controls. Payload Capacity -Minimum passenger capacity of six (6) personnel or an operational payload of not less than 1,000 lbs (453 kg) on cushion. Powerplant -Minimum 100 HP, multi-cylinder, liquid-cooled, fuel-injected engine with dual radiator cooling and electric start. Speed & Endurance -Minimum cruise speed of 35 mph; calm water speed greater than or equal to 45 mph; minimum operational range of 70+ miles on a standard fuel tank. Operating Temperature -Must function reliably across an ambient range of -30°F to +110°F (-34°C to +43°C). Buoyancy & Hull Safety -USCG-compliant positive flotation providing greater than or equal to 135% unladen displacement buoyancy with closed-cell composite urethane foam. Terrain Clearance -Minimum 8-inch hard structure obstacle clearance at operational hover power with segmented finger skirts. Emergency Integration -Factory-integrated emergency beacon/lightbar, siren/PA system, searchlight receptacle, and non-slip deck. Transportation & Deployment Requirements Dedicated Trailer: One (1) matching single-axle fly-on/fly-off tilt trailer equipped with hull-protection rollers and standard ball hitch. Rapid Deployment: The entire system must be capable of single-person launch and recovery from the trailer directly onto dry ground, mud, or water. Training & Technical Data Deliverables The contractor shall deliver: Operator Certification: On-site certified pilot training (Class 3 Pilot Certification curriculum) covering basic control, high-speed turning, reverse-thrust braking, and casualty extraction maneuvers. Maintenance Training: Factory or on-site maintenance instruction covering pre/post-flight inspections, skirt segment replacement, and engine servicing. Technical Manuals: Commercial operator, maintenance, and illustrated parts breakdown (IPB) manuals delivered at vehicle handover. System for Award Management (Sam.gov) registration is mandatory for this contract (see SAM website at (https://sam.gov/content/home). Responses will contribute to the Market Research Report as part of the acquisition strategy development process. Sources responding are invited to provide input and recommendations concerning contract type, contract clauses, and other aspects of the acquisition and anything else that may help to develop an efficient and effective acquisition strategy. If sufficient responsible and capable sources are identified, a formal RFQ will be posted on SAM.gov. detail.title: Speed Trailers
detail.description: The Government has a requirement for the procurement of two (2) 18-inch speed display radar trailers and two (2) 50-watt solar panels to keep them powered. Vendors are requested to provide a firm-fixed-price quote. The units must meet these salient characteristics: Radar and Display Characteristics: 18-Inch LED Digit Display: Ultra-bright, high-intensity amber (or multi-color red/yellow) LED characters that are highly visible from distances up to 1,000 feet. Radar System: Must be able to measure both approaching and departing directions (dual direction) with the ability to turn off or select one of those directions. 2. Power & Solar Configuration 50-Watt Solar Panel: Highly efficient monocrystalline solar panel mounted on a bracket to provide continuous trickle-charging to the battery bank. Battery Power Bank: Equipped with one (minimum) deep-cycle marine/AGM batteries (Group 24 or equivalent, around 80–100 Ah total capacity) to provide up to 7 to 14 days of autonomous operation without sunlight. Smart Charger: An onboard smart battery charger with an AC shore power outlet to recharge batteries manually when needed. 3. Construction & Physical Security Trailer Chassis: Built from rugged, heavy-duty welded steel tubing (typically 2-inch square 11-gauge steel) with a powder-coated, rust-resistant. Stabilization: Equipped with 3 or 4 retractable, adjustable jacks/stabilizers to lift the tires and secure the trailer in place, even in high winds. Vandalism Protection: Secure, lockable steel enclosure housing the batteries and controllers to prevent unauthorized access or tampering. Display Window: A durable, shatter-resistant, and UV-stabilized Lexan® or polycarbonate window protecting the LED face from road debris and vandalism. 4. Controller & Software Capabilities Local Controls: Push-button, rotary dial, or touchscreen local interfaces located in a locked enclosure. Automatic Brightness: Integrated ambient light sensor that automatically dims the LEDs at night to conserve battery power and brightens them during direct sunlight for visibility. Timers: Need auto shut off after an hour of usage in the event the unit is left on to prevent unnecessary battery drain, not necessarily a timing system with schedules.

Purpose The Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation) intends to issue a solicitation for a follow-on contract for the lease of two (2) prefabricated mobile structures in support of the Security Response Force Training Center (SRFTC), located approximately two miles downstream of Grand Coulee Dam near the Town of Coulee Dam, Okanogan County, Washington. detail.title: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) High-Capacity
detail.description: This is a Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (RAS) announcement. The Navy is pleased to announce the next marketplace opening for the Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) family of systems (FoS) program. The Navy intends to release a Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) by 01 August 2026. The RPP will include detailed requirements for high-capacity MUSV solutions used for logistics support and capable of transporting containerized payloads.MUSV uses modular design principles to create adaptable and resilient solutions that can effectively counter evolving threats. Interested parties with expertise in vessel construction, autonomy, perception systems and complex maritime problem solving experience are invited to participate in this opportunity. detail.title: Next Generation Undersea Security Initiative (NG-USI)
detail.description: Synopsis : This is a solicitation for parties interested in participating in projects sought by the Strategic Systems Programs (SSP) for state-of-the-art technologies and capabilities for the Next Generation Undersea Security Initiative (NG-USI). NG-USI is established to meet requirements in the following Focus Areas of Interest: Focus Area #1: Signal Mitigation – OPNAV/N975 Prototype technologies that may mitigate the generation, radiation, propagation, and scatter of a variety of signal types (acoustic, chemical, optical, electromagnetic, radiological, hydrodynamic, and cyber) associated with submarine and unmanned system operations, to include both peacetime and wartime operations. Focus Area #2: Comprehensive Counter-Unmanned Systems (C-UXS) – Nuclear Weapons Surety (NWS) & OPNAV/N975 Prototype technologies to detect, track, identify, deny, and defeat unmanned systems across all domains (aerial, surface, underwater, and ground). This area seeks scalable solutions for shore-based installations and afloat operations in Port, Harbor, Littoral, and Waterways (PHLW) and open ocean environments. (Examples include: kinetic/non-kinetic effectors, electronic warfare/jamming, and physical denial systems such as advanced netting or modular infrastructure shielding). Focus Area #3: Defeating Adversarial Autonomy & AI – NWS Prototype technologies to effectively counter hostile Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) capabilities. Solutions should focus on defeating autonomous swarms, disrupting AI-enabled Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) directed at nuclear facilities, and hardening strategic security networks against AI-driven cyber-physical attacks or spoofing. Focus Area #4: Next-Generation Electronic Security Systems (ESS) & Sensor Fusion - NWS Prototype and integrate novel Electronic Security Systems (ESS) to modernize perimeter and interior defense for strategic weapons facilities. Solutions must provide multi-layered intrusion detection, perform reliably in all weather conditions, significantly reduce false alarm rates, and seamlessly integrate into existing command and control nodes to automate alerts for response forces. Focus Area #5: Enhanced Access Control & Security Screening - NWS Prototype technologies for advanced personnel and vehicle screening to ensure rapid, zero-failure access control at strategic facility perimeters. This area calls for high-fidelity detection of contraband, explosives, radiological threats, and unauthorized surveillance devices without impeding operational flow and logistical requirements. Focus Area #6: Strategic Maritime Transit & Escort Security - NWS Prototype technologies to ensure the zero-failure secure movement of strategic maritime assets. This area seeks advanced maritime situational awareness, physical security enhancements for escorting SSBNs, and the detection, avoidance, and mitigation of maritime mines, and the defeat of direct-fire kinetic threats (e.g., shore-launched ATGMs/RPGs) during transit through PHLW to and from dive points. Focus Area #7: Strategic Ground Convoy & Land Transit Security - NWS Prototype technologies to ensure the zero-failure secure movement of strategic land-based assets. This encompasses advanced ground surveillance, secure tactical communications, vehicle tracking multi-layered physical security protocols, and Active Protection Systems (APS) to defeat direct-fire threats (e.g., ATGMs/RPGs) for ground transport and convoy operations of strategic weapons and equipment. Focus Area #8: Next-Generation Harbor & Expeditionary Surveillance - NWS Prototype technologies to establish persistent Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) for strategic ports and harbors. This area seeks advanced sensor networks tailored for the waterside environment. detail.description: AMENDMENT #1 issued 3 September 2026, see attached documents. The 101st MSC Office is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation for the procurement of wireless communications infrastructure materials, conduit, grounding equipment, and supporting electrical hardware in support of the SC GASNTi2 BLOCK 1 project. This procurement includes a mandatory requirement for a purchased ISO shipping container in which all materials must be delivered and stored. Upon acceptance of delivery, title and ownership of the shipping container will permanently transfer to the United States Government. All materials must strictly conform to the specifications outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW) and the attached List of Materials (LOM) (or approved "or-equal" equivalents). 2. INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS (FAR 52.212-1 ADDENDUM) 2.1. Submission Instructions Offerors must submit their quotes via email to the primary Government Points of Contact (POCs) listed below no later than September 18, 2026, at 5:00 PM EST . Late submissions will not be evaluated. 2.2. Quote Package Requirements The quote package must include the following distinct elements: Technical Quote: A completed bill of materials pricing sheet matching the item numbers in Attachments (LOM). Detailed product specification sheets for any proposed "or-equal" items, including a side-by-side comparison chart matching the salient characteristics defined in the LOM. Conformance statement confirming that all materials will be delivered palletized for forklift transportation within a new or highly refurbished ISO shipping container that will become the permanent property of the Government upon delivery. Price Quote: A firm-fixed-price (FFP) quote detailing unit and extended pricing for all LOM items. Crucial Pricing Note: The total cost of the ISO shipping container, including its initial freight and logistics, must be fully integrated and amortized within the unit prices of the delivered materials. No separate demurrage, retention, or container rental line items will be accepted. Representations and Certifications: Completed copy of FAR 52.212-3 (Offeror Representations and Certifications—Commercial Products and Commercial Services) or confirmation of an active and up-to-date registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). 3. EVALUATION AND AWARD CRITERIA (FAR 52.212-2) The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) . Quotes will be evaluated based on the following two factors: Factor 1: Technical Acceptability The technical evaluation will be graded on a Pass/Fail (Acceptable/Unacceptable) basis. To be rated "Technical Acceptable," the quote must demonstrate: Strict conformance to the exact part numbers specified in Attachment #1, OR technical data sheets proving 100% equivalency to all listed salient physical, functional, and performance characteristics for proposed "or-equal" substitutions. Unequivocal acceptance of all Statement of Work terms, including base security access, delivery terms, and the permanent transfer of ownership of the delivery/storage shipping container (SOW Section 2, Item 5). Factor 2: Price Pricing will be evaluated for fairness and reasonableness. Award will be made to the lowest-priced quote that has been determined to be technically acceptable. 4. The 87th Communications Squadron requires the procurement, delivery, and physical installation of one Class 5 Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) container and associated SIPRGuard accessories to provide secure housing and mass management of SIPRNet devices in Building 2320, Room 101, Joint Base MDL, NJ. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for this requirement at this time. Sources that believe they can meet this requirement are invited to submit a capability statement, including technical data and cost information, in sufficient detail and with convincing evidence to clearly demonstrate the capability to provide the required hardware, software, and installation services described below. GSA-approved Class 5 security containers of this type may only be purchased from the manufacturer identified on the QPL for that specific model; no other source is authorized to sell or install this item. In addition, the required SIPRGuard gateway modules, manual control module, and associated TrustedCare maintenance plans are proprietary products designed, manufactured, and supported exclusively by Trusted Systems, Inc., and are not available from any other source. Based on market research, there is reasonable evidence that Trusted Systems, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of furnishing this equipment and its associated installation and maintenance without substantial duplication of cost to the Government that could not be expected to be recovered through competition, and without unacceptable delay in fulfilling the 87th Communications Squadron's requirement. detail.title: Laboratory Analysis - Phase II Environmental Site Assessment - Fort DuPont, Delaware City, DE
detail.description: Introduction: It is the intent of the Government to award a sole source purchase order for analytical laboratory services from Alpha Analytical as cited in the attached Sole Source Justification. Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Departme nt of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Targeted Brownfields Assessments (TBA) Program. As part of this effort, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) that includes a requirement for laboratory analysis will be conducted at the Fort DuPont Parade Ground (the Site) located at 260 Old Elm Ave, Delaware City, Delaware. Background: The objective of this Phase II ESA investigation is to determine if known contamination stemming from former military operations at the Fort DuPont property has impacted soil or groundwater at the Parade Ground (OU-9). Laboratory analytical data from soil and groundwater samples obtained through the advancement of soil borings and the installation of groundwater monitoring wells will be collected. Analytical results will be compared the Human Health and Ecological Screening Levels published in the Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC) Hazardous Substance Cleanup Act (HSCA) Screening Level Table Guidance Appendix A tables. Soil samples will be compared to the Soil (Direct Contract) HSCA Human Health Screening Levels and the Ecological Surface Soil Screening Levels. Groundwater samples will be compared to the Groundwater HSCA Human Health Screening Levels. Tasks to be Performed: The Phase II ESA investigation includes the Contractor tasks listed below. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirements. 1) Sample Containers, Handling, and Delivery : The Contractor shall provide the appropriate sample containers, disposable volatiles samplers, preservatives, pre-printed labels, and analyte-free water required for the analyses listed below. These are to be delivered by the Contractor to the project site location. Sample collection and handling will be performed by Volpe personnel. The laboratory shall provide a daily local courier to transport the samples from the Site to the laboratory over an anticipated three days of sampling. Whenever possible, the Contractor shall minimize the number of sample containers by combining compatible analyses into a single container, as allowed by EPA methods and laboratory standard operating procedures. 2) Sample Analysis: Metals, Cyanide, VOCs, SVOCs, TPH-DRO, TPH GRO, PCBs, Pesticides, VOC Trip Blank, Metals, Cyanide, VOCs, SVOCs, TPH-DRO, TPH GRO, PCBs, Pesticides.

detail.description: See attached Solicitation. Here is the PWS: Performance Work Statement (PWS): Centralized Receiving and Shipping Point (CRSP) The contractor shall provide Two (2) appropriately trained, supply and services labor to establish, operate, perform, and manage centralized receiving and shipping point (CRSP). Work hours are 0700 1530, Monday through Friday (30min lunch alternating). CRSP tasks include issuing to personnel authorized by delegation of authority card, DA Form 1687 (electronic or manual form acceptable) maintained on file, receiving, unloading or diverting trucks, reviewing manifests, breaking out items, inspecting items, recording transactions, receiving push shipments, redirecting mis-shipments, inspecting, photographing and coordinating with the Installation Transportation Division (ITD). The contractor shall operate the Automated Manifest System (AMS). The contractor shall perform these functions in accordance with AR 710-2, DA PAM 710-2-2 AR 735-5. The contractor shall use material handling, motor transportation to distribute cargo to, or receive cargo from, other CRSPs, ports operations areas, or bases/camps in support of onward movement and retrograde. The contractor shall distribute and backhaul supplies and materials to supply activities on the installation. The contractor shall maintain complete visibility of all ISO containers moving to and from the CRSP and provide input to the Army Container Asset Management System (ACAMS). The contractor shall provide monthly Labor Hours worked per Attachment 0002 Hours Work Report. The contractor shall submit documents per the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) found in Attachments 0003 and 0004. detail.title: DLA Energy Fuel Transportation Services - Progreso, Yucatán, Mexico (JP5)
detail.description: 1. Notice Type This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market-research and planning purposes only . It does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ), solicitation, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses to this notice will not be considered offers, proposals, or quotations, and no award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. 2. Agency and Purpose The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is conducting market research to identify responsible commercial sources capable of providing fuel transportation, cross-border customs support, delivery, and offload services in support of U.S. Navy maritime operations in the vicinity of the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico. The anticipated support is for Southern Border operations in the vicinity of the Gulf of America. 3. Anticipated Requirement The Government anticipates a requirement for the contractor to furnish and deliver approximately 20,000 U.S. gallons of JP-5 from DFSP Houston to Progreso, Yucatán, Mexico , per delivery event. For market-research purposes, respondents should identify their ability to support recurring deliveries at the stated quantity and provide recommended delivery lead times. The method of transportation is not prescribed. Respondents may propose the commercial transportation method or combination of methods that most effectively, safely, lawfully, and reliably supports the mission, including tanker truck, ISO container, or another commercially available approach. 4. Commercial Delivery and Acceptance Concept The Government is seeking commercial solutions under which: The contractor shall provide transportation services for Government-owned fuel and perform all activities necessary to deliver and offload the fuel at the designated delivery point in Progreso, Mexico. The Government will accept the full delivered quantity during each delivery event. The fuel will be offloaded directly into a Navy vessel, as directed by the Government representative. The contractor shall provide all transportation, coordination, personnel, equipment, documentation, and services necessary to safely complete delivery and offload. Detailed fuel-quality, inspection, quantity-verification, acceptance, safety, environmental, and operational requirements will be established in the performance work statement (PWS) or solicitation. 5. Required Contractor Capabilities Interested parties shall have the ability to provide the following: Bulk transportation of JP-5 or comparable aviation/marine petroleum products via tanker truck, ISO container, or other suitable commercial transport capacity. Transportation from a Defense Fuel Support Point (DFSP) to Progreso, Mexico. Cross-border transportation operations between the United States and Mexico. Ability to properly coordinate delivery of fuel products the Port of Progreso and other applicable ports, terminals, piers, and local authorities. In-transit security and accountability for fuel from pickup through Government acceptance. All equipment required to transfer fuel at destination, including compatible hoses, couplings, pumps, grounding/bonding equipment, spill-response equipment, and calibrated/certified quantity-measurement equipment, as applicable. Ability to conduct fuel offload to shore-side receiving equipment and/or directly into a Navy vessel, as directed. Contingency and recovery procedures for transportation disruption, border delays, weather, equipment failure, fuel-quality discrepancies, or unsuccessful delivery/offload. 6. Requested Capability Statement Content Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement that addresses the following: Company information Legal business name. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, if applicable. Point of contact, title, business telephone number, and

detail.title: Safety Data Sheet (SDS) and Chemical Management System — Enterprise Subscription
detail.description: RFQ PCA-ORS-07827 — Safety Data Sheet (SDS) and Chemical Management System, Enterprise Subscription COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION (i) Description. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented by the information contained in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. (ii) Solicitation Number. PCA-ORS-07827. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). (iii) Provisions and Clauses. The solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular. (iv) NAICS / PSC / Set-Aside. This acquisition is full and open. The applicable NAICS code is 513210, Software Publishers . The Product Service Code is 7A20, IT and Telecom - Application Development Software (perpetual License Software) (v) Description of Requirement. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) requires a commercial, cloud-based Safety Data Sheet (SDS) and chemical management system supporting hazard communication, chemical inventory management, and regulatory compliance across NIH Institutes and Centers. The Government intends to award a single firm-fixed-price contract consisting of a 12-month base period and four (4) 12-month option periods . (vi) Performance-Based Statement of Work. Objective. The contractor shall provide an enterprise SDS and chemical management platform for up to 27 NIH Institutes/Centers with unlimited simultaneous users , including SDS library access, chemical inventory management, hazard classification, labeling, regulatory reporting, emergency response support, training, and implementation services. Minimum Performance Requirements. The proposed solution shall: Provide enterprise access for up to 27 NIH Institutes/Centers with unlimited simultaneous users. Provide access to a comprehensive supplier/manufacturer SDS library sufficient to support NIH chemical inventories, with continual updates at no additional charge. Allow users to search, locate, index, print, download, and share SDS from the vendor library and NIH-managed inventories, including searches by chemical name, CAS number, product/part number, and supplier/manufacturer. Provide SDS organization by user-defined folders or physical storage locations, version and archive control, and a complete audit trail. Notify users when supplier/manufacturer SDS are updated and identify material changes. Provide container-level chemical inventory management, including quantity tracking by volume or weight and automatic recalculation of applicable hazard classifications as quantities change. Support manual entry and barcode and/or RFID-based container management. Generate GHS-compliant labels and concise worker safety summaries. Generate regulatory and compliance reports, including SARA/EPCRA Tier II, RCRA, carcinogen, and hazardous substance reporting. Support creation and classification of chemical mixtures and control-banding risk assessments. Provide synchronized mobile access for iOS and Android to SDS, labels, inventory information, and emergency response information. Provide 24/7/365 chemical emergency response telephone support for NIH employees and authorized third-party contractors. Provide 24/7/365 customer support , access to an e-learning/training platform, implementation assistance, and administrator/user training. Implementation. The contractor shall provide onboarding and implementation support, including SDS population, registration, or migration services necessary to establish NIH's initial system environment. The quotation shall separately identify any implementation or one-time charges. (vii) Place of Performance. detail.title: BLU-138/B  Penetrator Warhead
detail.description: PURPOSE The U.S. Government (USG) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources for a potential BLU-138/B procurement. This effort will determine market competitiveness and assess the feasibility of a Small Business Set-Aside. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 332993 - Ammunition (except Small Arms) Manufacturing. This notice seeks industry feedback on capabilities, small business status, and preferred Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract lengths. Responses will validate acquisition strategy decisions. This is not a solicitation and does not guarantee a future contract. The Government encourages responses from all small businesses, including 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone, and Women-Owned. Interested parties should provide: Confirmation of small business status under NAICS 332993 Description of anticipated teaming arrangements, specifying roles of the prime and partners. Summary of relevant experience delivering similar services to government or commercial customers within the past three years DESCRIPTION The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center Armament Directorate, Munitions Sustainment Division, GBU Components Branch (EBHC), Hill AFB, Utah seeks potential contractors with the technical expertise to produce: BLU-138/B 5000 lb. Advanced Penetrator Warhead (EMPTY CASE) CNU-754/E Shipping and Storage Container Taper Ring Taper Ring Set Screws Explosive fill is not part of this requirement.
